item.title: ‘Occupation. Expulsion. Settlement’: Israeli politician campaigns on platform to ethnically cleanse Gaza
item.description:
‘Occupation. Expulsion. Settlement’: Israeli politician campaigns on platform to ethnically cleanse Gaza

Submitted by MEE staff on Thu, 10/08/2026 - 12:14
Zehut leader and former Likud MK, Moshe Feiglin, defends slogan as he calls for Israeli settlements to be built in the strip 
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (R) and Moshe Feiglin, far-right Zehout (Identity) party chairman pictured in 29 August 2019 (AFP)
Off

A former Israeli lawmaker has published election campaign adverts on public buses bearing the slogan: “Occupation. Expulsion. Settlement.”

Moshe Feiglin, chairman of the Zehut party, defended the slogan after it drew criticism online.

A longstanding advocate of expelling Palestinians from their homeland, Feiglin said on Instagram that people should get used to his policies.

“We will not delete a single comma. Take a very good look at these signs, because they are not going anywhere,” he said.

“You read it perfectly correctly, letter by letter: Occupation. Expulsion. Settlement,” he added.

Feiglin said his party would “settle” every inch of what he called the Land of Israel.

The hardline politician has built his political career around opposition to a peace agreement with the Palestinians. 

'As Hitler said, ‘I cannot live if one Jew is left’. We can’t live here if one ‘Islamo-Nazi’ remains in Gaza' 

- Moshe Feiglin, Israeli politician

He has advocated building the Third Temple on the site of the Al-Aqsa Mosque, annexing the occupied West Bank and Gaza Strip, and expelling Palestinians. 

Feiglin served in Israel’s parliament, the Knesset, from 2013 to 2015 as a member of the Likud party.

He left Likud and established Zehut in 2015.

Last month, he signed an electoral agreement with Bezalel Smotrich to merge their parties into a single bloc, ahead of the 27 October elections.

The move could secure him a seat in parliament if the alliance wins the projected five to six seats.

'Every baby in Gaza is an enemy'

Earlier this week, Feiglin told the Jerusalem Post that he wanted “to see Gaza empty”.

“Occupation, transfer all, all the Arabs. I don’t care. They cannot stay there after what they did,” he said.

He added that the entire population of Gaza, including babies and children, were the “enemy”, rather than just Hamas.

“The baby that will be born in Gaza tomorrow will do exactly the same [as the 7 October attack], God forbid, to your baby that will be born tomorrow in Jerusalem,” he said.

“There’s no other way. That’s the reason they live for. That’s what they learn with their mother’s milk.”

“You’re not going to change them. You’re not going to educate them,” he added.

"The enemy is Gaza, not Hamas.” Speaking to the Jerusalem Post, Israeli politician Moshe Feiglin said that the entire population in Gaza, children, are the “enemy”, while framing total forced expulsion, permanent annexation, and settlement in Gaza as a moral obligation https://t.co/9yWLSGyoTE

— Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye) October 6, 2026

Feiglin has made similar remarks in the past.

Last year, he said during an interview on Israel’s Channel 14 that “every child, every baby in Gaza is an enemy”.

“We need to occupy Gaza and settle it, and not a single Gazan child will be left there. There is no other victory,” he said.

In 2024, Feiglin invoked Adolf Hitler while calling for Palestinians to be expelled from the Gaza Strip, describing them as “Islamo-Nazis”.

“As Hitler said, ‘I cannot live if one Jew is left’. We can’t live here if one ‘Islamo-Nazi’ remains in Gaza,” he argued. 

Feiglin has also previously called for the “complete destruction of Gaza, before invading it ... Destruction like Dresden and Hiroshima, without a nuclear weapon,” in an interview with Al Jazeera in October 2023.

item.title: Supporters of Druze faction raise Israeli flags in Sweida on 7 October anniversary
item.description:
Supporters of Druze faction raise Israeli flags in Sweida on 7 October anniversary

Submitted by Reem Aouir on Thu, 10/08/2026 - 11:48
Protest in Syria highlights growing ties between followers of Hikmat al-Hijri and Israel
Cars in Sweida show images of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Syrian Druze leader Hikmat al-Hijri (X/Screenshot)
Off

Supporters of Druze spiritual leader Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri rallied in the southern Syrian city of Sweida on Wednesday in solidarity with Israel, marking the third anniversary of the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023.

Footage shared on social media showed participants carrying Israeli flags and portraits of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu alongside pictures of Hijri.

Many Druze men also took part in a car procession through the city before gathering in al-Karama Square, according to local reports.

The vehicle used at the front of the procession appeared to carry Israeli licence plates and participants carried banners reading “We will not forget, we will not forgive”.

The Hamas-led attack on southern Israel killed around 1,200 people, and 251 were taken hostage.

Israel's subsequent genocide in Gaza has since killed at least 74,250 Palestinians and wounded 175,278, according to the Palestinian health ministry.

That total includes at least 1,445 people killed since a ceasefire took effect in October 2025.

Images from Wednesday's protest also showed photographs of people killed in the 7 October attack alongside images of those killed during violence in Sweida.

Rejecting 'extemism'

Wednesday's rally was promoted two days in advance by groups affiliated with the National Guard, an armed coalition linked to Hijri.

In a post on Facebook, a page called “The al-Sumoud Battalion” issued the call for residents to attend what it called a solidarity rally to “honour victims and reject extremism, massacres and violence against civilians”.

“We remember the victims of massacres and violence against civilians in Israel, just as we remember the victims of the massacres in Jabal al-Bashan [southern Syria].

“We face the same phenomenon: extremism and religious and political violence practised by political Islamist groups,” the group said.

The organisers sought to draw a parallel between the 7 October attacks and the violence that took place in Sweida in July 2025, using the slogan "The massacres are many, and the perpetrator is one".

The rally comes amid increasingly close public ties between Hijri and Israel.

Israel has repeatedly presented its intervention in southern Syria as an effort to protect Syrian Druze. During the violence in Sweida in July 2025, Israel struck Syrian government targets, saying it was acting to protect the Druze community.

Pictures of Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa were seen burnt and ripped while one protester was quoted by local journalists as saying: “We can no longer live with the government of terrorism and extremism of Damascus… Our loyalty lies with those who protect our existence.”

Seven killed in Syria after gunmen open fire on bus in Homs
Read More »

Another protester said: “We stand against terrorism, which is something shared within all these organisations, like Tahrir al-Sham, Ahmad al-Sharaa or the Syrian government.

“Our stand today is humanitarian against the terrorist attack that happened to us in Jabal Bashan or the attack of 7 October.”

Many protesters thanked the government of Israel and Netanyahu, who they claimed was fighting terrorism.

According to Suwayda 24, a local news page, Rami Ashti, Nawras Azzam and Ghaith Kantar, leaders of Hijri's security office, attended with dozens of armed members.

The protest drew criticism from local sources and many Syrians online who condemned the gathering and said the participants did not represent the province's wider population.

Many said solidarity should instead go to the thousands of children Israel has killed in Gaza.

Sweida has held several pro-Israel rallies since July 2025. That month, fighting between Druze factions, Bedouin tribes and government forces killed almost 2,000, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights.

item.title: Ed Miliband insists UK will 'build back up' presence in Jerusalem as British consulate closes on Israel's orders
item.description:
Ed Miliband insists UK will 'build back up' presence in Jerusalem as British consulate closes on Israel's orders

Submitted by Imran Mulla on Thu, 10/08/2026 - 10:20
Britain has opted not to expel Israeli diplomats or defy Israel's orders
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband speaks during the Labour Party's annual conference in Liverpool, Britain, 28 September 2026 (Phil Noble/Reuters)
Off

Britain has announced it is closing its consulate in occupied East Jerusalem and downgrading its building to the status of a mission, ignoring calls to defy Israel's orders.

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar gave considerably different messages in separate statements issued on Thursday morning, the deadline Israel had set for Britain to close its consulate.

Miliband said the UK would not retaliate against Israel over the closure but would work to "build back up" its diplomatic presence in East Jerusalem.

Saar declared: "The British Consulate in Jerusalem is ending its operations today. Accordingly, the sign of the British Consulate in Jerusalem has been removed."

He said that on Wednesday night the Israeli government had reached an understanding with the UK: "The building that served as the Consulate is the property of the British Government.

"We have allowed the British Government to operate a task force of only seven diplomats from the building, which ceased to function as a consulate today. Their scope of activity will be very limited."

In his own statement, Miliband said: "We have been clear that we do not accept that the Government of Israel has the legal right to close the British Consulate General in Jerusalem, which has been there for nearly 200 years."

He added that the UK "reiterates" its view that East Jerusalem is occupied Palestinian territory. Significantly, the UK last month recognised Israel's occupation as illegal.

Miliband said "our Consulate General building will not be closing, and will be known as the UK Mission, Jerusalem from today."

He insisted the mission "is independent, operational, and will continue to deliver vital services and our work with the Palestinian people".

The foreign secretary further said "the UK has temporarily withdrawn a number of staff and families to ensure their safety and security."

A less strident approach

Middle East Eye revealed on Wednesday that the British consul-general to Palestine, Helen Winterton, was expected to leave Jerusalem, but that a "skeleton crew" might remain at the consulate.

NAZA: Israeli embassies in UK and US promote rival documentary to challenge Gaza genocide allegations
Read More »

Saar announced the order to close the British consulate last month in retaliation against the UK’s move to ban trade with Israeli settlements.

The announcements on Thursday come after the British government faced calls - including from Emily Thornberry, chair of parliament’s influential Foreign Affairs Committee - to defy Israel and refuse to close the consulate. 

Israeli media reported earlier this week that Britain was preparing to expel Israeli diplomats and their families from London in retaliation for the closure. 

Instead the UK has ultimately opted to take a significantly less strident approach. 

MEE understands that Britain's decision was being watched closely by other consulates, including France and Spain, which fear they will be next to be forced out if the British quit.

Britain has two diplomatic missions to Israel and Palestine: the embassy in Tel Aviv and the consulate for Palestinians, based in the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood, where residents have faced years of threats of eviction and settlement expansion.

Many Palestinians have told MEE of the importance of the work of the British consulate in providing witness to human rights abuses and reporting them back to London in a way that the British embassy in Tel Aviv cannot.
